info.title: NUnit Console Runner (.NET Core
info.description: The dotnet command-line runner for NUnit

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription:
By default, this command runs the tests contained in the
assemblies and projects specified. If the --explore option
is used, no tests are executed but a description of the tests
is saved in the specified or default format.
Notes:
1. The --where option is intended to extend or replace the earlier
--test, --include and --exclude options by use of a selection expression
describing exactly which tests to use. Examples of usage are:
--where:cat==Data
--where "method =~ /DataTest*/ && cat = Slow"
Care should be taken in combining --where with --test or --testlist.
The test and where specifications are implicitly joined using &&, so
that BOTH sets of criteria must be satisfied in order for a test to run.
See the docs for more information and a full description of the syntax
information and a full description of the syntax.
2. Several options that specify processing of XML output take
an output specification as a value. A SPEC may take one of
the following forms:
--OPTION:filename
--OPTION:filename;format=formatname
--OPTION:filename;transform=xsltfile
The --result option may use any of the following formats:
nunit3 - the native XML format for NUnit 3
nunit2 - legacy XML format used by earlier releases of NUnit
Requires the engine extension NUnitV2ResultWriter.
The --explore option may use any of the following formats:
nunit3 - the native XML format for NUnit 3
cases  - a text file listing the full names of all test cases.
If --explore is used without any specification following, a list of
test cases is output to the writer.
If none of the options {--result, --explore, --noresult} is used,
NUnit saves the results to TestResult.xml in nunit3 format.
Any transforms provided must handle input in the native nunit3 format.
3. If the --agents option is specified, the runner will not load any tests
until an agent is available. Consequently, it is not possible to provide
a count of the tests to be run at the start of the run. The count included
in the <start-run> event will be zero in this case. This has no effect on
the console runner's execution of the tests but may cause a problem for
extensions that rely on that field to display progress information.
4. To be able to load NUnit projects, file type .nunit, the engine
extension NUnitProjectLoader is required. For Visual Studio projects
and solutions the engine extension VSProjectLoader is required.

options.name: --test
options.description:
Comma-separated list of NAMES of tests to run or
explore. This option may be repeated.

options.name: --testlist
options.description:
File PATH containing a list of tests to run, one
per line. This option may be repeated.

options.name: --where
options.description:
Test selection EXPRESSION indicating what tests
will be run. See note 1 below.

options.name: --param
options.description:
Followed by a key-value pair separated by an
equals sign. Test code can access the value by
name. This option may be repeated.

options.name: --testRunTimeout
options.description: Set timeout for the entire test run in MILLISECONDS

options.name: --testCaseTimeout
options.description:
Set default timeout for each test case in
MILLISECONDS. May be overridden with
TimeoutAttribute.

options.name: --seed
options.description: Set the random SEED used to generate test cases.

options.name: --workers
options.description:
Specify the NUMBER of worker threads to be used in
running tests. If not specified, defaults to 2
or the number of processors, whichever is
greater.

options.name: --stoponerror
options.description:
Stop run immediately upon any test failure or
error.

options.name: --mainthread
options.description: Run tests on themain thread.

options.name: --wait
options.description: Wait for input before closing console window.

options.name: --work
options.description:
PATH of the directory to use for output files. If
not specified, defaults to the current directory.

options.name: --output
options.description: File PATH to contain text output from the tests.

options.name: --result
options.description:
An output SPEC for saving the test results.
This option may be repeated. See note 2.

options.name: --explore
options.description:
Display or save test info rather than running
tests. Optionally provide an output SPEC for
saving the test info. This option may be
repeated. See note 2.

options.name: --noresult
options.description: Don't save any test results.

options.name: --labels
options.description:
Specify whether to write test case names to the
output. Values: Off (Default), On, OnOutput,
Before, After, BeforeAndAfter. On is currently
an alias for OnOutput, but is subject to change.

options.name: --extensionDirectory
options.description:
Specifies an additional directory to be examined
for extensions. May be repeated.

options.name: --test-name-format
options.description:
Non-standard naming pattern to use in generating
test names.

options.name: --trace
options.description:
Set internal trace LEVEL.
Values: Off, Error, Warning, Info, Verbose (
Debug)

options.name: --enable
options.description: Enables the specified extension. May be repeated.

options.name: --disable
options.description: Disables the specified extension. May be repeated.

options.name: --noheader
options.description:
Suppress display of program information at start
of run.

options.name: --omitignored
options.description:
Suppress listing of tests not run because they
were ignored.

options.name: --omitexplicit
options.description:
Suppress listing of tests not run because they are
explicit.

options.name: --omitnotrunreport
options.description: Suppress the entire report of tests not run.

options.name: --nocolor
options.description: Displays console output without color.

options.name: --help
options.description: Display this message and exit.

options.name: --version
options.description: Display the header and exit.

options.name: --encoding
options.description:
Specifies the encoding to use for Console standard
output, for example utf-8, ascii, unicode.

options.name: --config
options.description:
NAME of a project configuration to load (e.g.:
Debug).

options.name: --configfile
options.description: NAME of configuration file to use for this run.

options.name: --framework
options.description:
FRAMEWORK target runtime to use for tests in the
form of a TFM, e.g. net462, netcoreapp3.1, net8.
0. If not specified, tests will run using the
target runtime for which they were compiled, if
available, or the best installed version, if not.

options.name: --mono
options.description:
Run tests using the Mono implementation of the .
NET Framework.

options.name: --x86
options.description: Run tests in an x86 process on 64 bit systems

options.name: --dispose-runners
options.description:
Dispose each test runner after it has finished
running its tests.

options.name: --shadowcopy
options.description: Shadow copy test files

options.name: --loaduserprofile
options.description: Load user profile in test runner processes

options.name: --skipnontestassemblies
options.description: Skip any non-test assemblies specified, without

options.name: --agents
options.description:
Specify the maximum NUMBER of test assembly agents
to run at one time. If not specified, there is
no limit. See note below.

options.name: --debug
options.description: Launch debugger to debug tests.

options.name: --pause
options.description: Pause before running to allow attaching a debugger.

options.name: --list-extensions
options.description:
List all extension points and the extensions for
each.

options.name: --list-resolution-stats
options.description:
Display usage of each ResolutionStrategy in
loading .NET Core assemblies.

options.name: --set-principal-policy
options.description: Set PrincipalPolicy for the test domain.

options.name: --debug-agent
options.description: Launch debugger in nunit-agent when it starts.

options.name: --debug-console
options.description: Launch debugger in nunit-console when it starts.
